To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nuclear localization of Hsp90 is associated with high MHC-class-I expression and susceptibility of tumor cells to CTL-mediated apoptosis.

(a) breast cancer cells with high MCH class I expression show increased nuclear localization of Hsp90; (b) this correlation is not observed in cells with low MHC class I levels; (c) these data suggest that nuclear Hsp90 may be a factor involved in the regulation of MHC class I gene expression in breast cancer cells.

1) the 90 kDA heat-shock-proteins (HSP90s) are elevated in breast cancer; 2) HSP90s are localized in the nucleus of tumor cells; 3) nuclear HSP90s correlate with MHC class-I expression and 4) HSP90 is involved in apoptosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new molecular mechanisms of breast carcinogenesis.
the identification of a molecular mechanism by which tumor cells escape CTL-mediated apoptosis.
the role of HSP90 in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nuclear HSP90 is involved in the MHC class-I pathway and that the HSP90 is an essential component of the nuclear MHC class I pathway.
the nuclear localization of Hsp90 may be a marker for MHC class I upregulation and resistance to CTL mediated apoptosis in human breast cancer.
nuclear HSP90 expression may be a prognostic marker for MHC class I and thus for a CTL response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nuclear accumulation of HSP90 is associated with high levels of MHC class I protein expression and that this may be a mechanism to prevent apoptosis in tumor cells.
the nuclear localization of Hsp90 is associated with MHC class-I expression in breast cancer cells.
the HSP90 expression in the nucleus is a new prognostic marker for MHC class I.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nuclear HSP90 may be an important target for future immunotherapy of breast cancer.
the nuclear localization of Hsp90 is associated with the expression of MHC class I.
the nuclear HSP90 may play an important role in MHC class I mediated tumor cell apoptosis.
